ledger.note: 1815, 9 June: the Final Act of the Congress of Vienna makes "most of the Duchy of Warsaw, except the provinces held by Austria and Prussia" an "independent Kingdom of Poland" with Tsar Alexander I as king (128,500 km2 and about 3.3 million people at creation; the Tsar agreed the compromise on 24 October 1815 and the constitution was adopted 27 November 1815).

sources.note: Final Act 9 June 1815: most of the Duchy of Warsaw becomes a Kingdom of Poland; Prussia receives the western parts (Posen), Gdansk; Austria Tarnopol; Krakow a free city; compromise 24 October 1815.

notes: No Cliopatria row: the land lies in Cliopatria's Duchy of Warsaw (1809-1813), Free City of Krakow (1815-1845) and Russian Empire shapes. Typed colony (a kingdom in personal union with the Tsar, then a Russian province). The shape is a reading: Duchy of Warsaw 1812 less Greater Poland and Krakow, which gives a ratio of 0.97 to the page's 128,500 km2. Not on the pages: the dates of the Krakow free-city treaty and the Posen boundary, the Torun and Danzig cuts, the Bialystok district (Russian since 1807), the fall of Warsaw (August 1915) and the Act of 5 November 1916. Names the gazetteer lacks: Chelm (Kholm). Counterparts: duchy-of-warsaw exists (eu-20); free-city-of-krakow exists; the German-established Government General of Warsaw and the Military Government of Lublin have no dossier.
